slides.title: Scientific Presence, Measured Like Market Share
bullets: Measures how present and credible a company's scientific voice is
Compared relative to competitors within a therapy area
The medical-affairs equivalent of commercial market share
Built on scientific credibility and presence, not sales volume

slides.title: Good Data Can Still Lose the Conversation
bullets: A company can have excellent clinical data and still lose ground
This happens if competitors are more present where opinion forms
Advisory boards, congress symposia, guideline committees, publications
Increasingly, digital scientific content and communities too

slides.title: Signals That Combine Into Share of Voice
bullets: Presence and visibility at key scientific congresses
Publication output and citation performance versus competitors
Participation in guideline development and advisory processes
Digital engagement and reach across scientific communities

slides.title: Every MSL Shapes This Metric Directly
bullets: Trust-building scientific exchange contributes incrementally
So does every insight that sharpens the evidence-generation agenda
Advisory board facilitation also contributes
Thin or inconsistent engagement lets a competitor's voice dominate

slides.title: Why Consistent Presence Still Matters
bullets: A quiet quarter is not just fewer visits
It can mean scientific presence in that network is losing ground
This framing justifies sustained field presence beyond any single visit

takeaway.title: Share of scientific voice measures a company's scientific credibility against competitors
bullets: It is built from congress presence, publications, advisory input and digital reach
Individual MSL activity directly shapes this metric in the field
Consistent presence matters even without one dramatic outcome per visit
